To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a human endogenous provirus on chromosome Xq 22.3 encodes a truncated envelope protein, which is detected by a monoclonal antibody.
we identified a new, partially defective human endogenous retroviruses (HERV)-like env gene on chromosome Xq 22.3 and showed that it can produce a truncated Env protein.
a defective human endogenous retroelement can encode a truncated envelope protein that is detectable in human tissues by an antibody.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the protein product of a partially defective HERV env gene located on the long arm of chromosome X, which may be of relevance for understanding the biology of HERV-W.
the identification and characterization of a new HERV-W env locus on chromosome X and the protein encoded by this locus.
the possibility that defective HERV loci may be capable of encoding incomplete HERV proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a defective HERV-W element on chromosome Xq 22.3 can produce an N-terminus truncated protein, and this truncated protein is detectable by the monoclonl antibodies 6A 2B2 and/or 13 H5A 5.
N-Tren is a HERV-W Env-like protein that is produced by the Xq22.2 HERV-W env locus and is detected in vivo in placenta and brain.
a partially defective HERV locus on chromosome X has retained coding capacity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that a defective HERV-W locus on Xq22.2 is expressed in human peripheral blood and that it produces a truncated HERV-W protein.
the Xq22.2 HERV-W env locus, which we propose be renamed ERVWE2 (endogenous retrovirus with env), is transcribed and can produce a truncated env protein, named N-trenv.
the Xq22.1-2.2 locus is a HERV-W locus that encodes a truncated envelope protein and is expressed in multiple sclerosis lesions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HERV env genes are much more complex than previously assumed.
, contrary to what was believed, HERV env genes can encode proteins even when they are interrupted by stop codons.
the N-terminus of HERV-W Env plays an important role in the protein’s structure and function, and that the HERV-W Env N-terminus is dispensable for oligomerization.
